reviews.text: The cinematography, sound design, and editing is as elegant as you’d expect from Cuarón. Not enough good things can be said about Yalitza Aparicio and her performance too, a stunning performance for a non-professional.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Roma is a riveting, gut-wrenching, and utterly absorbing experience that completely floored me.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Cuaron does a wise thing by not keeping this story too close to the chest; it's not strictly autobiographical, and serves as his interpretation of what Libo may have experienced, but more importantly the motherly qualities he always saw in her.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Alfonso Cauron’s most personal film of his career is his most visual striking film since Children of Men.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: ...This is no coincidence since Roma represents the portrait of a canonical family model that also collapses, which is also consistent with the prominence of an earthquake during one of the most significant scenes of the feature film.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: that is Cuarón’s true magic: when the film is over, although we don’t know exactly how and when it happened, a little part of his Mexico somehow belongs to us too.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: Watching Alfonso Cuaron's Roma is almost like flipping through a beautifully-shot album of 1970s Mexico.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: There’s a deep emotion that comes with the territory and a boldness that is rarely seen and Cuaron, along with a brave performance from Yalitza Aparicio.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: It truly is a movie of detail with each gorgeous black-and-white shot framed like a richly detailed memory begging to be examined.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Cuaron is a master filmmaker who creates true hyperrealism with Roma, a front seat to everyday life. It’s admirable in its approach and beautifully photographed, but there is an emotional disconnect that can’t be shaken.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Roma is the sort of film described as life-affirming without irony or pretense, as it reminds us of the potential for love, frailty, and unbreakable bonds between people.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The keen and sensitive understanding of what the lives of women are what Cuaron displays here, and deploys with such enormous empathy...
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Roma deals in complicated subject matter - socioeconomic inequality, broken families, loss - but never in a way that dehumanizes its characters or detracts from the power of its central story.
reviews.author: Betsy Bozdech

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuaron's masterful Roma is a semi-autobiographical epic that reminds us that cinema is art.
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: Roma will be studied for years as a landmark in cinematic storytelling, made even more meaningful because it pays tribute to a character who is usually in the background.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: A staggering swirl of life, a film that destroys and uplifts simultaneously.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: In her first feature film debut, Aparicio gave a performance that though quiet in execution, was powerful.
reviews.author: Carolyn Hinds

reviews.text: Roma represents a major shift in the movie world.
reviews.author: Nathan Mattise

reviews.text: Without a doubt the most essential film of Cuarón's career, and obviously, his most personal
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Roma is a sweeping-yet-intimate story that deserves to be considered among the best of the year, whether you watch it in the theaters or on Netflix.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: A stunning piece of personal cinema.
reviews.author: Sophie Charara

reviews.text: Roma is not a film that can be explained - it's a film that needs to be felt.
reviews.author: Jim Rohner

reviews.text: The beach sequence encapsulates everything Cuarón has been working for - pairing technical virtuosity and universal human decency to a maximum impact. Quietly spectacular, this larger format, digitally shot film needs to be seen on the big screen.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: I'm sad to say that I didn't love it as I wanted to. But I do admire it completely.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: This is a movie from the point of view of the housekeeper, usually a secondary character that doesn't have a voice [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: [Yalitza] Aparicio's work is of staggering power.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: The subjects are incredibly un-cinematic, as his camera documents - in a somewhat documentarian style - the lives and lifestyles of painfully average people.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Aesthetically, the film is gorgeous. Cuaron has an attention for detail that other filmmakers should study.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Transcendent.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Perhaps the true mastery of the film is that it never actually feels like a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Cuarón's work as a writer, director and cinematographer are beyond perfection. His use of chaos to create the ordinary are the work of a genius. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: A slow-burn film that recalls the Italian Neorealist movement. The goal is a slice-of-life character study rather than plot twists, but if you flip your mental switch, it's a subtly enveloping film that elicits nostalgia.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: The result is the most novelistic and experiential offering yet for [Cuarón], but make no mistake: Roma is not a film of gimmicks.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Cuarón has a crafted something that is purely, assuredly human.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: It doesn't happen often, but sometimes as a film critic you exit a film so extraordinary and emotionally stirring that words nearly fail you. Writer/director/cinematographer/co-editor Alfonso Cuarón's deeply personal work Roma is just such an experience.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Each moment, each dialogue build toward something very special, and then, the movie takes your head, looks you in the eyes and inspects your soul. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Gorgeous and formally flawless, the director's precision and meticulous craft is unmatched, and his deep, personal connection to the story readily shines through. Roma is all of these things, but it also left me absolutely cold.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: It's a beautiful, emotional, human film, without music, which recreates an era with great aesthetic meticulousness and dissects the inequalities between social classes in a particular period of Mexican sociopolitical history. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: In Cuarón's films, cinema conjures up its own world, and this one provides the chance to explore it with him more intimately than ever before.
reviews.author: Kathleen Sachs

reviews.text: The movie's distance here works against it, emphasizing its outsider's view of what it frames as lower-class concerns. Instead of lending her character dimensionality, Cleo's tribulations begin to feel cartoonishly grim.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: Roma is intimate, epic and female-focused, not unlike filmmaker Alfonso Cuaron's 2013 intergalactic 3-D odyssey Gravity... But Roma is also an immersive nostalgic valentine to his '70s childhood in Mexico City.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: Fundamentally, it's a character piece about Chloe. Aparicio's placid, yet expressive face sometimes recalls Renée Falconetti in The Passion of Joan of Arc. Hers is a brilliant, unmannered performance.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's most masterful film contains multitudes.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: By paying homage to his childhood, [Cuarón] has created a simple yet jaw-droppingly beautiful film that can only be seen as one thing: a visual masterpiece.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The surround system is equally sublime, simulating action not seen on the screen, giving the film a transportive, immersive feel.
reviews.author: Redmond Bacon

reviews.text: This is less a plot-driven film than a cinematic experience of being transported back in space and time. To a place in memory where anything can still be a marvel and the ordinary is sacred.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: "Roma" is the year's most gorgeous film too, capturing people and places with stunning clarity and intimacy.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: It struck me as remarkable that a film of this prestige and calibre contained such an honest, direct message - you're much stronger than you think you are, even if nobody cares to notice it.
reviews.author: Rhys Tarling

reviews.text: This film is a masterpiece of storytelling and filmmaking.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: [Roma] pays attention to the overlooked, the lowly, the humble -- the things a utilitarian, power-obsessed world disregards or merely uses.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: If the streaming giant's theatrical rollout finds its way to your vicinity, you owe yourself the unique experience of sitting down in a seat in order to walk through someone else's memory. It's like nothing you've ever heard or seen.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: 'Roma' is Cuarón's most personal work: it is raw and hopeless, but, above all, very beautiful. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Álex Manzano

reviews.text: In this amazing representation of atmospheres, the work the Production Design team delivers is effective and very innovative. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: A complex and wrenching exploration of privilege and class relations that cuts deep with a kind of sharp naturalism that recalls De Sica and a haunted magical reverie worthy of Fellini.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Roma's script is an artisanal delight: Full of symbolism and mysteries with harmonious results thanks to the characters' journey. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: The clarity of the film's images is like a slap to the face confronting us with a past that is at times too much to bear.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: I couldn't help but marvel and wonder if this was what it must have felt like to be among the audience to see Vittorio de Sica's Bicycle Thieves or Michelangelo Antonioni's L'Avventura for the first time.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Rooted in Cuarón's memories, Roma is a love letter to the woman who raised him and the city he called home.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Much of the narrative plays like a cinematic diary of Cleo's day-to-day life; the camera, a compassionate observer thoughtfully taking note of the moments of transcendence within the ordinariness of a life of devoted service.
reviews.author: Antonio Sison

reviews.text: The fact is, the film really just needs to be seen to fully appreciate Cuaron's artistry in making the everyday seem profound.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: If you can see it on the big screen, you'll be rewarded. Partly because it looks so great, and partly because it's a sedate film that needs a real investment by the viewer.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: The astounding size of the purse to promote "Roma" paid off with a nomination and other awards, but it buys me little appreciation except for the downright beauty of the black and white imagery.
reviews.author: Jules Brenner

reviews.text: Roma is an impressive cinematic achievement: a revolutionary movie for contemporary mexican cinema and an intimate reflection on Mexico City's history, sounds, divisions and feelings. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Ruiz

reviews.text: The black-and-white spectacle captures the memory of childhood, in unflinching clarity.
reviews.author: Poulomi Das

reviews.text: A beautiful glimpse into middle class malaise in 1970s Mexico, Cuarón shows an affinity for the simplicity of life then and the complexity that often creates waves.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Breathtaking cinematography captures the most anxious, harrowing, loving, even banal moments and bathes them in shimmering beatific light. But Roma also insists on being a narrative. And that requires more than just pretty pictures.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: You will have to wait for things to get going but, when they do, this film becomes a tapestry of emotion executed in sublime style.
reviews.author: Phumlani S Langa

reviews.text: It's beautiful story, he shot it himself along side writing and directing, at this stage we can see it in a bunch of different places, its on Netflix & in theaters, but go see it in theaters!
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: An incidental thread that serves as an excuse for the director to capture on screen an amalgam of memories and a veritable whirlwind of sensations on the surface. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Stories like [Cleo's] are often erased from history, and it is a painful joy to see them told with dignity and loving detail.
reviews.author: Danielle Burgos

reviews.text: Roma, from writer/director Alfonso Cuarón, is a warm and loving memoir to Mexico City, where he grew up and was cared for by women who loved him and his siblings.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: There is sadness and some humor in Roma.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: To Roma's credit, Cleo is not a sidekick or played for laughs. She's in the foreground.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Aparicio, in her acting debut, is remarkable.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: A beautiful yet unromantic look back at Cuarón's childhood, and a gorgeous tribute to the woman who helped raise him.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Kudos to Cuaron for crafting such a visually-captivating, surreal memoir of his troubled coming of age!
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Roma essentially has no plot, but it doesn't need one. Cuarón has reached back into his memories and made a finely crafted tribute.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Cuaron's love of long takes - demonstrated so masterfully in Children of Men & Gravity - allows you to soak in all the subtly placed detail about the lives of these people...his understated use of the camera engineers some great cinematic moments.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: As it stands, it's a beautiful film that's so preoccupied with creating a realistic, immersive world of sights and sounds that it forgets to make its central character an actual person.
reviews.author: Britt Hayes

reviews.text: There'll be plenty to write about Roma in the days to come aside from this brief reaction, but I'm so excited for you to get to see this film: It's truly astonishing.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: It's a piece of cinema that, whilst mostly grounded in the mundane, finds the grandeur and cinematic potential in every conceivable moment.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: While "Roma" is a deeply personal expression of one man's childhood memories, I responded to it, from today's climate, as a very affecting way of viewing a woman's dilemma of work versus motherhood.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: The director, Alfonso Cuaron, brings the audience into the world of his childhood in Mexico City's Roma neighborhood through masterful blending of the intricacies of power dynamics in class, ethnicity, politics, family and gender.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: despite being gorgeously shot and genuinely earnest in its drama, it is too much in Cuarón's head
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Both intimately small and sweepingly epic.
reviews.author: Jack Blackwell

reviews.text: The result, albeit a masterpiece, is a textbook example of the male gaze and the inflated masculine ego behind it.
reviews.author: Laura McPhee

reviews.text: Cuarón has made more entertaining movies for sure, but none so heartfelt and even soulful.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Every frame of the film could be isolated and hung on a wall, and maybe that's what should be done with it. "Roma" is a beautiful boring movie.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The simple and realistic storytelling discloses individual complexities that made me care for these characters with all my soul.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Could a Netflix movie win the best film Oscar come February 24? You better believe it.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's Roma is a soulful cinematic prayer. It's an open letter which embraces and reverences childhood, class struggles and politics.
reviews.author: Niall Browne

reviews.text: For all of the highlights on Cuarón's resume, Roma sees the director enter another realm.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: ...a masterful endeavor from a seriously talented filmmaker.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Cuarón fills every corner of the frame, just as Fellini did, so that the eye has to roam the screen as though scouring a fresco. But for all the bustle and brio, it's a visually lucid movie.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: It is ravishingly shot and at times deeply moving.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: However easy it is to dismiss a static or slow camera as performing attentiveness, it works - I have never looked so hard at soapsuds.
reviews.author: Phoebe Chen

reviews.text: It feels like something students will be studying in film school for many years to come and yet unlike many arthouse pieces it made me cry. I was invested in these people and their lives
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Cuaron is a bit too close to the material, and most moviegoers will have to do a lot of research to truly get and appreciate the movie. Still, a true work of art.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: With beautifully profound storytelling, strong characterizations, meticulous attention to period detail and heartfelt direction, Roma is one of the best films of 2018 and it deserves all the praise from critics.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Yalitza Aparicio underacts so wonderfully, does so little with words, that we almost always know what her character is feeling: when she is contented, entertained, worried, frightened.
reviews.author: Michael Wood

reviews.text: Roma is an act of understanding-an investigation by Cuarón of where he came from, and of what and who made him-and it's moving in the way that an honest and generous investigation of that kind can be.
reviews.author: Caleb Crain

reviews.text: So much happens in Roma. It is so bursting with life, Mexican life.
reviews.author: Alma Guillermoprieto

reviews.text: This has plenty to say about class relations too, but what's most impressive about it is how the Mexican writer-director-cinematographer-editor transforms even his political observations into the stuff of big-screen spectacle.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: This time, it's personal.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: There are many memorable images in the film that stuck with me after the film was over. Roma is full of life and love -- ordinary, down to earth people in extraordinary circumstances.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Roma builds to a celebration of simple virtues that are so undervalued in the current socio-political climate... And Cuarón observes these values in practice, with artistry and perception.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: If it wasn't clear before, then Roma is a gorgeous guarantee that achieving technical perfection is Alfonso Cuarón's one true goal.
reviews.author: Aaron Leggo

reviews.text: Set in the comfortable upper middle-class neighbourhood of Roma in Mexico City, this compelling story centres on a marriage slowly splintering apart and the native Latina live-in maid who stands at the swirling heart of the family for whom she works.
reviews.author: Karen Krizanovich

reviews.text: Haunting, poetic, and a film impossible to forget.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Given Cuaron's stunning wide-screen black-and-white cinematography and the film's meticulous Dolby Atmos sound design, Roma is definitely worth a trip to the theater, but mostly, it just quietly demands to be seen.
reviews.author: Brandy McDonnell

reviews.text: There is no cloying dialogue, or artificial moments and characters. Every moment is real.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: Small in scale but enormous in its emotional impact, this drama from one of Mexico's top film-makers is a masterclass in how everyday events, shot in a natural, unforced way, can make for gripping cinema.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: I feel like Roma is a perfect example of how a director can re-examine aspects of their life and people who influenced their life without turning everything into a stereotypical mess.
reviews.author: Monique Jones

reviews.text: Like a great dish made out of the fewest, purest ingredients.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Shot in black and white (Cuarón served as cinematographer as well as writer and director), it's an intense memory piece, dealing with the challenging subjects of class, race, and gender, in an evolving country without preaching or even taking a side.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Oscar-winning writer/director Alfonso Cuarón's breathtakingly poignant and personal Roma will move you to the core.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Powerful because it is so personal. Cuaron is drawing from his own life to portray the Mexico of the 1970s he remembers. Filled with social hierarchy and political unrest.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: The amount of praise the film has received is not justified because the story is mediocre and feels very pretentious. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: Cuaron is masterly in building up a climax without any plot virtuosities or overt stylish broad brushes.
reviews.author: Sanjukta Sharma

reviews.text: Roma is, for better or worse, Cinderella for the 21st century. It's a powerful film, beautiful and compelling, but to what ends is difficult to say.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: The thing that Cuarón chooses to highlight the most is the strength of women, and how they are left to pick up after the messes that men make and refuse to take responsibility for.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: Moving quietly through a year in Cleo's life and using beautiful black-and-white cinematography, the film is deeply emotional but rigorously unsentimental.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Cuarón's camera switches back and forth from long, deliberate takes interspersed with short, action-filled sequences. The black and white photography is simply gorgeous and exactly right for the story.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón doesn't so much recreate his childhood in the Colonia Roma neighborhood of Mexico City as he reimagines it...
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Roma stars a Oaxacan woman of color who pierces the idea of a nebulous Latino or Hispanic identity.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Even for someone as accomplished as Cuarón,  Roma  stands out as one of more remarkable pieces of filmmaking in recent memory.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The detailed artistry is outstanding, but visionary flair coupled with poignant authenticity doesn't necessarily make an entertaining movie.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Maybe the masterpiece of Alfonso Cuarón. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A movie like Roma is rare - something that's intimate yet also grand.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Having broken through the haze of childhood memory, Cuarón knows that those forces of power - and the race, class, and gender dynamics they set in motion - define the complex intimate relationships between domestic workers and their employers.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: Roma is the kind of movie that comes just a few times in a generation and forms part of a canon of masterpieces.
reviews.author: Indra Arriaga

reviews.text: A film that deserves to be seen by anyone who cares about cinema.
reviews.author: Adrian Hennigan

reviews.text: Director Alfonso Cuaron has made a full-on masterpiece with this heartbreaking, semi-autobiographical knockout.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: If Alfonso Cuaron's Roma could be reviewed in one line, it would be this: Give the Oscar out now and save us all staying up late next year.
reviews.author: Chris Newbould

reviews.text: Above all else, Roma is an extraordinary visual experience.
reviews.author: James Greenberg

reviews.text: A cinematic valentine to a Mexican maid whose kindness has a positive impact on all those around her.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: By making Roma so specific to his own memory, Cuarón has created a mesmerizing, powerful, universal story.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuaron's heartfelt ode to the Mexico City of his childhood and the women who influenced him is unlike any other movie you will see this year. That's a good thing.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: It offers an increasingly rare combination of ambition, imagination, compassion, emotion and execution.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Cuaron brings new definition to what is considered a "spectacle". Indeed, Roma is spectacular.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: A complete experience, merging an offering of love and empathy with the sharpness of large-scale filmmaking, presented in a way few could pull off like Cuaron.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: An incredibly emotional story, which manages to perfectly convey the social differences that exist in countries like Mexico. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Worth seeing in any format, Roma is best when viewed on the biggest possible screen with the least amount of distractions.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: For all its worthy intentions, "Roma" is little more than the righteous affirmation of good intentions.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: In Roma, Cuarón has crafted not just a great feat of cinema, but a work that's destined to be savored and pored over for decades to come.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: Roma captures, as well as any film I have seen, the spirit of "magical realism," without ever hinting at the supernatural. Its magic is pure, stunning cinematic technique.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: It is a highly emotional and enthralling love letter...
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: The personal connection of Alfonso Cuarón with the story moves to the screen in such a way that everything looks endearing and familiar. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo Fernandez

reviews.text: I urge you to enjoy it on a big screen and more importantly as part of the communal experience that film - and especially this film - is meant to be.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: It highlights how such projects can be used for self-reflection that's actually relevant to society. If it can be used to examine privilege, then it can lead to striking, honest works of beauty such as Roma.
reviews.author: Jonathan Victory

reviews.text: The art direction in Rome is amazing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Yes. It's a remarkable film, both intimate and epic, that is moving and often surprising.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: Sometimes this feels like artifice, but the emotions are real enough, and Cuaron's tribute to Cleo, and to women like her, is heartfelt.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Childhood memories are powerful markers of identity and experiences; thanks to"Roma"for evoking such while one is unaware, as it works magic in creating new imagery to sustain them.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: While the film portrays the larger picture of Mexico's sociopolitical issues, above all else, it's a personal movie.
reviews.author: Kylie Madry

reviews.text: This is an exceptional movie, powerful and stark, and beautiful.
reviews.author: Russ Fischer

reviews.text: Cuaron's signature long takes immerse the viewer in this environment, the camera slowly panning to drink in the details of this world he's recreated from his memory.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: ...the vast majority of movie-goers will not find Roma accessible at all...another "critic" movie that applauds abstract art and serves in-part as Cuaron hero-worship.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: There is quite simply no other film like this being made right now, and few directors with the reach and ability to achieve it.
reviews.author: Tom Augustine

reviews.text: I can't recall another art movie so openly patronizing toward its subject, yet so self-flattering of its maker's largesse.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: A vivid exploration of the world Cuaron came from and is bound to be a signature achievement for the director, who has managed to put together a captivating film that is thoughtful both in substance and style.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Crafted with stunning detail, [Cuarón] infuses substance into each scene.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: There isn't much talking in Roma, nor are there many close-ups of the characters - faces and words are forgotten as time passes; and Alfonso Cuaron wants his film to feel like a half-remembered dream, washed away by the tide of time.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Cuaron's memory movie is a beautiful thing, and he does some fine camerawork as well.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: A powerful piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: It's a slice of life. You just watch everything unfold and it's beautiful.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: I felt bad for the dog.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: This Netflix original lacks agency within its' character beats that have a frustrating passivity to the narrative. [Alfonso] Cuarón's film comes to the brink of being cruel to its setting and characters.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Cuarón is dangling a cathartic hook as Cleo 'overcomes' personal tragedy with a heroic gesture. But the whiff of injustice still lingers at the film's end - to me, at least.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Roma isn't just a film, it's a tidal wave of empathy with an undeniable sense of momentum, worth watching on the biggest screen you can find.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: A stellar and brilliant visual experience and deeply moving tale...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: It's a love letter to mothers when all is said and done: biological and otherwise. And it succeeds in large part due to a stunning debut performance by Aparicio.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: This is a film that is more fun to study than to be entertained by. It may be art but it is not great entertainment.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Roma is small life drama writ large.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's edgily political black-and-white epic of a family in 1970s Mexico City is as masterfully choreographed as Children of Men but more personally intimate.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: A series of beautiful, gorgeous shots stitched together that excellently mask a thin story and largely uninteresting characters - Yalitza Aparicio aside.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuaron's new film, "Roma," gives you so much to see in each new vignette, in every individual composition, in fact, that a second viewing becomes a pleasurable necessity rather than a filmgoing luxury.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It doesn't matter how you see it; Alfonso Cuarón's latest is a movie that turns you inside out, revealing a personal story on a grand scale.
reviews.author: Lindsay Zoladz

reviews.text: Perfection. Cinema doesn't get as rich as this.
reviews.author: Cameron Frew

reviews.text: Roma is, hands down, in the top cinematic tier.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Cuaron obviously is one of the boys in this on-screen family, but Roma isn't about children or even childhood; it's a movie about a moment and the people who lived it.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Aparicio had never acted before taking on the role and that raw talent makes her mastery of character all the more remarkable - if ever a film proved that the camera can read minds it's Roma.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Roma unfolds so naturally, so realistically, and so affectingly that it's best seen and heard on its own terms. So see it big, and see it loud.
reviews.author: Erik Henriksen

reviews.text: Pristine imagery carries this gorgeous-looking, but small and sleepy tale from Oscar-winning director Alfonso Cuaron. His very personal story, in fact, might not connect as easily as his camera.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A feat of filmmaking so accomplished it borders on showing off, but also a deeply rewarding piece of filmmaking...
reviews.author: Joe Reid

reviews.text: "Roma" is magnificent.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: It's an emotional roller coaster full of wonder and sorrow that feels like Cuarón rediscovering distant memories from his own childhood.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It's visually and auditorily captivating, pushing your emotional understanding to its limits.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: At-once nostalgic and fresh, Roma finds transcendence in the mundane moments of everyday lives and ordinary people ... It is a beautiful celebration of peoplehood and place in an often place-less world.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: If you don't allow yourself 135 minutes this weekend to soak it in, we can't be friends.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: A textbook example of Roger Ebert's description of cinema as an empathy machine, opening a window onto a world most of us would never otherwise know even existed.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Alive in a way that few movies are, "Roma" is a sumptuous piece of filmmaking, a gorgeous look at life on a grand scale told through the prism of one family.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: A generous and lovingly made film.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: We are all passengers on this beautiful trip down memory lane at the invitation of Cuarón. Oh, how lucky are we who can accompany him. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: Roma is an exciting look at family dynamics, a fascinating record of a convulsive time, an exploration of class differences, prevailing sexism, and contained violence. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Beautifully photographed and masterfully directed, Roma is Alfonso Cuaron's most personal and emotional film to date. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Roma, the film of the year, is an exquisitely tender work, and a deeply layered historical re-creation.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: A powerful, beautiful personal odyssey.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The images may be truly breathtaking to behold, but cinema requires more than mere beauty. There is no there there, merely a vacant (if splendid) filmic vessel.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: This beautiful new movie-probably the best of the year-is far more than a collection of memorial fragments.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: You allow the movie's sights and smells to envelop you in a world surrounded by turmoil and tragedy but held together by love and loyalty.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Roma demonstrates that great filmmaking can work on us almost subliminally, narrowing the distance between us and the screen.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's Roma is a magical film that weaves memories of a childhood as idyllic as it is raw... in a world where silences prevail in homes accompanied by the endless murmurs and din of the streets. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Cuarón does not conjure up nostalgia or false sentiment. He mixes personal melodrama with epic scale, creating gripping sequences where normalcy suddenly experiences tectonic shifts.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: Roma is Cuarón's love letter to his nanny, to his mother, to his siblings, and to Mexico. It's as pure as cinema can get.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: A marvelous film and definitely one of the best of 2018. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Roma is the sort of movie filmmakers and critics love, and audiences have to endure. Alfonso Cuarón's semi-autobiographical effort plays like a home movie that runs on and on, seemingly without organization or end.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Roma is more impressive as a feat of crowd control than as a piece of visual storytelling or as a character study; it's a film that's easier to admire than to fall in love with.
reviews.author: Philip Concannon

reviews.text: Roma is one of the year's best movies.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Cuarón pens a brilliant and touching love letter about Mexico City, family and motherhood. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Narratively, not a lot happens during the opening 60-70 minutes, but Cuaron is marinating us so that later events have an uncommonly strong impact.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: It's been such a long time that I've really seen a movie like this.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: It's a beautiful film that doesn't have to overstate its affection for the experience that the director had.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: In spite of everything, the director achieves in Roma the difficult feat of evoking the past with one foot in nostalgia and the other in the critical sense. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: Rome is a striking example of how a filmmaker can use all the tools at his disposal to tell a story full of humanity and heart, involving the viewer and bringing him closer to a temporary cut with much to analyze. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: Cuarón's film is quotidian and extraordinary at the same time. It is about change and how we adapt and grow. It is about love and sometimes the lack of it. It is a rapturous magnum opus, that is heartbreaking, devastating, and life affirming all at once.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Told through the impassive eyes of a live-in maid, it's the slow-moving and apparently autobiographical story of a middle-class family enduring earthquakes, bad parking and marital separation.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: "Roma" is the cinematic equivalent of poetry, full of moments gentle and traumatizing, with a focus on people's lives that can feel precise and small and monumental all at the same time.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Cuarón captures tiny moments in exceptional detail, finding the humor and tears in the everyday.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Roma has wonderful performances that wring the emotions and great visual beauty. It's a slow-burning masterpiece that deserves to be seen on a big screen.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: [Alfonso Cuarón] has done almost archaeological work to paint rather than represent the experiences, the way of life. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Roma is in a league of its own in terms of sheer cinematic ambition and prowess, but as a drama it's not as deeply moving as some of this year's very best.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: Roma tackles political context, race, ethnicity, and social class and although it manages to slip into the ethnic menial labor trope through its character Cleo, it does present an artful depiction of the social underclass through visual metaphors.
reviews.author: Jamie Broadnax

reviews.text: Filmed in glorious black and white, 'Roma' is another Alfonso Cuarón cinematic masterpiece.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: This is the kind of film that makes you look at the world differently; makes you see those things that felt previously inconsequential.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: "Roma" is a movie only in name. It's more an aural and visual experience that envelops your body before penetrating your soul.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: A pretty but unsatisfying arms-length experience.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's new film is the rare family drama that's also a feast for the eyes.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Roma's not cold, but it is calculating. You can almost feel Cuaron pulling your strings, a jealous deity happy to make you squirm in your seat while you beg for mercy.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The key to "Roma" is the patiently quiet and soulful performance by Aparicio.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón completes the movie of the year in one of the most beautiful tours of the wound of time. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: It is the clarity of Cuarón's eye, and the sea-like sway of his remembrance, that compel you to trust the tale he tells.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Rome, in fuction to Mexico, is timeless. It happens in the seventies, but it's also happening out there, right now. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: The way Cuarón accumulates details-the jumble of clothes drying on a roof, a broken jug after a New Year's toast, the ubiquity of the Jesus Christ Superstar soundtrack in 1971-builds an elemental power.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Ambitiously gorgeous and deeply personal, Roma is one of the best films of the year and deserves your full, undivided attention.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: Art-house aficionados and most critics will fall prey, like me, to the mesmerizing and apparently haunting look and feel of the production that has yet to leave my memory. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Nudity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Alongside fascinating social observations and surprising outbreaks of humour, Roma features one or two of the most heart-wrenching scenes in recent cinema.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A milestone of a movie, an epic, an event ... It is a film of constant compassion and absolute humanity. It is totally, essentially personal to Cuarón, but it is also fundamentally universal. It is filmmaking of the highest order.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: With virtuoso visual and sonic expression, Roma is a symphonic masterpiece that is sure to marvel for decades to come.
reviews.author: Caroline Madden

reviews.text: This is a film that alternatively shows humanity in all its ugly glory as well is its quiet moments of beauty.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: Immerse yourself in this beautiful memoir of growing up in early 1970s Mexico City from Academy Award winner Alfonso Cuaron shot in widescreen black-and-white. Yalitza Aparicio is glorious.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Nothing much happens, yet there is so much to watch.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: The term "masterpiece" gets chucked around far too loosely, and I mostly try to avoid it. But once in a lucky blue moon, there really are no other words to do a film justice.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: [I]t is admirable that Cuarón has chosen to see this familial and social change and violence from Cleo's perspective and through her experience.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: In its calm compassion, it's the antithesis of cynicism.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: From a visual and technical standpoint, it contains moments in which all of the elements of cinema come together with such precision that it puts most of the big ticket spectacles of recent years to shame.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A rapturous memory-piece, gorgeously shot and hypnotically paced...best experienced on the big screen, where its visual splendor and emotional resonance can be fully appreciated.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: After a while the self-conscious virtuosity becomes overbearing. It feels like taking an aircraft carrier to go around the corner to CVS.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: In the end, the film belongs to Aparicio, whose unmannered performance gives Roma an extra dimension of poetic realism.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: "Roma" achieves the rare feat of making the personal authentically political, not through explicit polemic or tortured metaphors, but simply by observing life with enough perspective to reflect it in all its contradictions.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Oh, how gentle, wide, wise, and true this movie is!
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: brings empathy and joie de vivre that is impossible to experience in the disposable world of the streaming age.
reviews.author: Dov Kornits

reviews.text: The beauty of this achievement is undeniable.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Cuarón's artistry yields a film with the pinpoint authenticity of a docudrama, but also the intoxicating and lyrical poetry of memories as filtered through a perfect dream.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's masterpiece oscillates between the intimacy of the director's Y Tu Mamá También and the grandeur of a Cecil B. Demille epic. It's an exquisite work of art filled with compassion and beauty
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Be thankful Roma exists. It's a special masterpiece, from a special, masterful filmmaker.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: A moving and empathetic glimpse at the mundanity and innate intimacy of domesticity.
reviews.author: Garrett Mitchell

reviews.text: ...suggests that in everyday domestic chores, strange and beautiful miracles are being performed.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Everyday, unpretentious, beautiful in its harshness, raw in its calmness, Rome is pure truth, it is cinema in capital letters. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: Roma is the sort of movie that successful pop filmmakers say they'd like to use their clout to make but almost never do.
reviews.author: Nick Pinkerton

reviews.text: Cuarón's wonderful eye is not limited to his formal decisions with the camera and photography, but also in the intelligence of putting a new actress at the forefront. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Shot in black and white, starring a nonprofessional actress, and set in a time and place seldom explored in mainstream cinema, "Roma" tells a deeply humane, enchanting story that easily ranks among the best and most indelible of 2018.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Few films this year impacted me more than "Roma."
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Every moment, every character is impeccably realised on-screen using skilful cinematography (by Cuaron himself), delightful production design and clever effects that recreate the period.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: What's become abundantly clear, over the course of this extraordinary run of searing films, is the degree to which Cuarón roots dramatic power in empathy and humanity.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Dogs everywhere. Human cannonballs... The occasional earthquake. A street massacre... There is blood and birth and gunfire and the eternal pull of the ocean itself, the great, sweeping, amniotic yet deadly sea.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: I can tell, Cuaron has directed a masterpiece, not just an intimate epic - an epic about intimacy.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Cuarón has successfully captured a sense of time and place resulting in a film that is as gorgeous as it is poignant, making it a cinematic experience not to be missed.
reviews.author: Paula Farmer

reviews.text: Cuarón has made a roster of impressive films...but "Roma," though perhaps not as immediately accessible, is his masterwork, a heartfelt evocation of a time and place that celebrates the unsung and the unheard.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: If you thought space would be Alfonso Cuarón's crowning achievement in terms of visual and auditory flair, think again; Roma is unforgettable and mesmerizing; bring the Kleenex
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Although it's quietly domestic in focus, Roma carries the heft Cuarón has gained in his Hollywood years, and wears it well.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: A bravura evocation of time and place, as richly detailed as the artfully designed worlds of Children of Men or A Little Princess.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A rare sense of transcending time and space is apparent while watching director Alfonso Cuarón's autobiographical drama Roma. It is arguably his most mature and delicate work to date.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: Roma is not so much a memory piece but a corrective to memory. It will become more harrowing before it ends, but love will triumph in an ocean ending that's more oceanic than anything I've experienced in the movies, and maybe in life itself.
reviews.author: Amy Taubin

reviews.text: There is a richness to Roma that will likely take multiple viewings to absorb.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Roma will be tough to beat as the best film of 2018.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuaron's poignant, neo-realist masterpiece that's best viewed in theaters.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Cuaron is an auteur in his own right, and as such puts his stamp on his own life's story. But in doing so, he never picks the stamp up, too often letting shots linger far longer than they are interesting.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: Roma is an unequivocally perfect film by every possible metric.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: An intriguing study in human dynamics and an exploration of how important certain people are who come into our lives during a formative time.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: A tribute to female solidarity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Huidobro

reviews.text: It's among the best work from one of the best filmmakers in the world.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: For those patient enough to allow Cuaron tell his family story will also see a story of love and heroism.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Roma doesn't seek to present a rosy solution, nor does it pass judgement. It's concerned with the details, the small things that make up a life and make it meaningful. Everyone matters in Roma - but especially those who so often get overlooked.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: Nothing happens that doesn't happen every day and everywhere across the world, or across its higher realms of social injustice and inequality. But the story seems special because the director's gaze is special.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Mexican director Alfonso Cuarón's Roma is a childhood memory film, both beautiful to look at and intriguing to contemplate.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón has made a truly inspiring, heartening and utterly devastating film. An absolute masterpiece.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: The film is reminiscent of Italian neorealism, yet Cuarón's shimmering black and white deep focus camerawork sets it apart...like having someone else's memories transferred into your brain, so acute is the sensation of nostalgia...
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A rare kind of masterpiece from director Alfonso Cuarón.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: It's clear how much Cuarón, who also wrote the script, cares for these people, and his passion and empathy immediately become infectious.
reviews.author: Brandon Katz

reviews.text: Cuarón's compositions... are works of art in movement. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The same techniques with which Cuaron made Gravity and Children of Men immersive experiences work for Roma's more intimate drama.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Cuarón has made his most personal film and his most universal, a modern masterpiece.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: "Roma" had wrapped me in its spell that completely, it would be hard to imagine a more artful arthouse attraction.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: Cuarón brings in eastern philosophy, mysticism, reflected planes, dog poo, an unusual amount of water and other confounding and wondrous things. It is vibrant, compassionate and profound but to describe it seems wrong, it must be experienced.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: 'Roma' literally took my breath away. It is a masterwork by one of the world's most versatile filmmakers, and will be justifiably praised as the best film of 2018.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Cuarón has explored the stylistic routes of realism and Roma extends the search. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: A textured, richly-detailed dream; a sympathetic memory of maternal grace that's anything but the placid surface it presents.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: A poetic, crystalline visual glory, demonstrating Cuaron's graceful, effortless, yet complete command over light, space, and rhythm. It recalls films like 'Sunrise' and 'The Night of the Hunter...' But thematically, it's all Cuaron's.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The focus is almost always on Cleo... At its best, this film makes you feel as if you could watch her go about her life forever and never tire of its simple, sorrowful dignity.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's Roma opens with a magic trick... Ta da. You could do it at home, if you wanted. The rest of Roma, I'm not so sure.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Roma is arguably the most ambitious and thrilling movie of the year - maybe of the decade, or at least since Cuarón last made a movie, 2013's Gravity.
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: Cuarón depicts these small moments with cinematic virtuosity, filming in rich black and white -- the director did his own cinematography -- with long continuous takes.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: ...the greatest film Alfonso Cuarón has made.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: An exhilarating masterpiece, Roma is at once quintessentially Mexican and profoundly universal.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: To see "Roma" is to be in awe of Cuaron's gifts and to wonder how he does what he does.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: It's as close to cinematic poetry as you can get and director Alfonso Cuarón, with an expert-level attention to detail, places us at the center of his story - watching, listening, waiting, and cherishing every delicate moment.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Just put the phone away, and allow yourself to submit to the serene, transcendent experience that is Roma.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: This is cinema that breathes with life and all its losses and discoveries. It is as enrapturing as a good story, and when it's over you think about it in the way you remember a dream.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: A mesmerizing, monochromatic epic that has to be experienced on the big screen.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: Pairing thrilling technical prowess with profound artistic vision, Alfonso Cuarón has made a masterpiece, at once understated and otherworldly. We need more filmmakers like him.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: One of the best things a movie can do is force us to settle down, quiet ourselves, and live inside someone else's experience for a while. And Roma is a shining example of a film that succeeds in that endeavor.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It's an expansive, emotional portrait of life buffeted by violent forces, and a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Like any art at its greatest, Alfonso Cuaron's autobiographical drama lets us see things we have seen before in a way we may never have seen them before.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A gorgeous love letter to an alternately cloistered and turbulent childhood.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: You rarely see such an intimate tale painted on such a large canvas.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Echoing in some ways the classics of Italian neo-realism, especially in its use of black and white, it is an epic of everydayness, as polished a personal film as you are likely to see.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Cuarón has composed some of the most stunning shots and sequences in film history, and it would be a sin not to see this on the big screen, if possible.
reviews.author: Yolanda Machado

reviews.text: Cuarón has done more than break through walls of language, culture and class to craft the best movie of the year. No matter how you see or stream Roma, this game-changer is making its own kind of history.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The result is a little too rose-tinted an homage, but Roma is still an exceptionally moving story, as well as another technical feat from Cuarón.
reviews.author: Danette Chavez

reviews.text: Roma's sound design is so amazing from the very moment that the film begins to appear on screen.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Roma is hypnotic and transporting and sublime, everything a movie seen on the big screen ought to be.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Having only watched Roma once, I'm not quite ready to declare it an all-out masterpiece, but it is a powerful, emotionally resonant work of cinema.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Yet another impressive technical accomplishment for Cuarón, Roma explores the filmmaker's memories of childhood in a truly immersive and vivid manner.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: Though often too wrapped up in memory to confront the hard questions, Cuaron's passion shines through in Roma to create a feature that's splendidly arranged.
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: Roma is achingly beautiful. What begins as subtle and nuanced, evolves into heartbreaking resolve. Alfonso Cuarón delivers another cinema masterpiece.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A breathtaking travelogue through the profundity of memories, "Roma" exhales the magic and empathy inherent in the very best which film has to offer.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: The brilliant film chronicles a middle-class family in the 1970s.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: This is perhaps the major cinema experience of the year so far.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: It's undoubtedly one of the greatest movies of 2018, destined to live on as a highlight of Cuarón's career.
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: If you appreciate the exquisite, melancholy beauty of the lives that bookend Roma-that bookend our collective stories-you will never forget this film
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuaron delivers his best film since Children of Men.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Roma is about memory, not fragmented and venerated, but realized with all its imperfections. As well as being an essential viewing experience, this is probably Cuarón's greatest film to date.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: Of those [films] I managed to see, none could match the clarity of vision and intensity of feeling, expansiveness and intimacy, breadth and breath of Alfonso Cuarón's Roma.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Roma does not disappoint. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Rosales Santos

reviews.text: The film is exquisite. It is a masterpiece and we will be talking about its artistry for years to come. My one recommendation this gift from Cuaron on the big screen.
reviews.author: Jazz Tangcay

reviews.text: This is a profoundly cinematic film, astonishingly beautiful, with one memorable shot or sequence after another.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: I look forward to returning to Roma once more, as I'm positive I'll find even more to appreciate. I only regret that my second viewing won't take place in a theater, where the towering images and visceral sounds fully mesmerize the senses.
reviews.author: Josh Martin

reviews.text: Plenty of movies are personal and don't come close to the feeling we get fromRoma, that we are literally walking through Cuaron's fondest memories.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The harrowing-at-one-moment and pastoral-the-next artistry may be compelling all on its own, but it's the weighty emotional heft of this film that shatters with resounding empathy to celebrate the resilience of special women.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Breathtaking, commanding, thought-provoking, epic and powerful, Roma is both a potent, cinematic and anti-cinematic ode to life and family that demands repeat viewing. A strong contender for film of the year.See it on as big a screen as/if possible.
reviews.author: Daniel Goodwin

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuarón's Roma is one of the films of the year, brilliantly observed and with an intense sense of yearning, lyricism and emotional truthfulness running through its every frame.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: A stunning achievement of cinema and not only the best film Netflix has released, but it is Cuarón's crowning achievement.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: Rarely do we critics allow ourselves to call a film a work of art, but that's the only turn of phrase for something as unforgettable and astounding as Roma. A cinematic masterpiece. Period.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Though there is a dramatic story arc, both for the family and for Cleo, Roma functions most superbly as deeply human vignettes of everyday life.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Yalitza Aparicio is the prophecy that the cinematic Gods spoke of, and the one we've waited for decades.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Roma is a film that relegates politics to its proper place. Cuarón's women understand that what matters most is what happens in your family, not this week's march in the streets. It's a useful insight, maybe now more than ever.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Roma is, overall, a quiet film, stable and calmly alert even when the volatility onscreen goes, within minutes, from zero to 100.
reviews.author: Natalia Winkelman

reviews.text: High drama is handled by the characters with equanimity, as Cuarón creates glorious, complex images that may, without context, sound precious, but in the film play as realistic details.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Stunning in black and white, the film contemplates the ways in which Cleo's bond with her employers can seem almost familial and the ways in which it emphatically isn't. She is both never alone and always alone.
reviews.author: Linda Holmes

reviews.text: Rome is complicated, emotional, [with] entertaining moments, perfect technique, but above all, is beautiful. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Cristina Vales

reviews.text: this is a film all about memories and is told through beautiful black and white visuals and precise grounded storytelling.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: What is the best way to see writer/director Alfonso Cuarón's reportedly semi-autobiographical ROMA? Definitely on the big screen, for which this gleamingly beautiful-looking film was exclusively designed.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: I was hypnotized and drawn in by the skill and heart of everyone involved.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: A great movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: Nothing sounds forced in the director's exquisite description of that world of yesterday, everything sounds true, his formidable visual language serves to express feelings and feelings with complexity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Roma feels grandiose, but it stays grounded in a powerful and personal story that pulls all the right strings at the right moments to make you feel like you've known this family your whole life.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: Aparicio provides color in the smallest, yet most tantalizing spectrum. She provides the hues that are rarely valued but should be taken for silver and gold. She provides the pallet of the everyday.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: A moving, ravishing, heartbreaking ode to the Mexico... This is a film so sincere and beautiful that, ideally, it deserves to be seen on the cinema screen. How about that, Netflix?
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: Social unrest can be felt all around the film's 135 minutes, and there are scenes that stay etched in your memory; that is what "Roma" is about, memory. It's not necessarily driven by plot as much as by these immaculately detailed moments.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Cuaron builds the symbol of a country that has killed their own future, a country that gives a face to the outside when inside, others tirelessly wash the blood spilled or avoid, there, the tragedy of the middle class. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Roma is autobiography as autocritique, and in exploring a point of view adjacent to his own, Cuarón appears to have rediscovered his identity as a filmmaker.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: There's hardly a frame in Roma that doesn't make you sit up and take notice. No matter how mundane the action on the screen is, Alfonso Cuarón turns it into something reverential.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: ... evinces a hyperrealism achieved not through visceral technique that interprets verisimilitude as hectic impressionism, but rather as the extreme density of historical and social observation of everyday things made monumental...
reviews.author: Daniel Kasman

reviews.text: Shot in arresting black and white and gorgeously crafted, the film is marred by a very slow, meandering Act I that barely holds attention.Then Act II launches into a melodramatic plotline that becomes engaging.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: It is the unique aspects of Rome, and not the invariables, that illuminate something about reality for which the sun has been insufficient. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Guilhem

reviews.text: Roma is a slow but steady immersion that, for the most patient and least distracted viewer, will sweep you away in a vision that turns mid-20th century domesticity into a 70mm epic.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Roma is hardly plot focused; it is almost entirely driven by emotion. This is clearly a passion project for Cuarón, and the result is a deeply moving melodrama about the quiet personal tragedies that unfold behind closed doors.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: An absolute classic. Will be taught in film schools someday.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: [Roma is] a majestic feat of filmmaking, an intimate portrait of a family that also serves as a broad portrait of a changing nation. Cuaron creates such a vibrant world that it demands to be seen on the biggest canvas possible.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Throughout the film, Cuarón's cinematography and editing tells a story of isolation and subordination-women and men framed and shot separately.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: Roma represents a certain kind of cinematic peak, where on both production and story grounds we're treated to something that nears perfection the way that only the truly great works do.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: Brilliantly conceived, beautifully acted, politically aware, and profoundly true-especially about the labyrinthine emotional relationship between domestic workers and their masters.
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: When looking to the past of history books or our own memories, individuals can recede into the fabric. Roma refocuses our attention...
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Executed to near perfection, this movie serves as a nostalgic time capsule of Mexico in the early '70s. Every performance is alive and intriguing.
reviews.author: Joelle Monique

reviews.text: By capturing and exploring Cleo's individual life with such vision and thoughtfulness, he has managed to piece together a sweeping interpretation of life itself.
reviews.author: Sarah Kurchak

reviews.text: Thoroughly absorbing and gently touching, ROMA opens a window into the past and has the feel of an Italian neorealist classic.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: A masterful achievement in filmmaking as an empathy machine, a way for us to spend time in a place, in an era, and with characters we never would otherwise.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: This is a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Cuarón's attention to detail is sublime.
reviews.author: Samantha Edwards

reviews.text: The film will deservedly receive attention for its autobiographical examination of social hierarchy, but the artistry is simply lacking...
reviews.author: Theo Schear

reviews.text: In its deceptive simplicity and indisputable beauty, the picture presents a strong refutation of policies designed to stoke xenophobia. It's an empathy machine.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: "Roma" is one of the best movies I've ever seen, and one of the most moving. If Norma Desmond had been able to see it she wouldn't have worried about the pictures getting small.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Roma is something special.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Cuarón impeccably links the personal and the political into dense scenes that reproduce the sudden yet inexorable nature of trauma; through his use of plans-séquence, he interweaves the individual and the collective, the private and the public.
reviews.author: Jennifer Lynde Barker

reviews.text: Cuarón's masterful artistry is what makes Roma personal, unique, and more visually striking than any film you've seen in quite some time.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

reviews.text: Roma may only span a year or so, but somehow in that year is the entirety of life itself - its small, fleeting moments of joy and longer, more poignant stretches of heartbreak.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: A richly textured masterpiece, Roma is cinema at its purest and most human.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Roma also makes the case that a great director possibly becomes greater if he serves as his own cinematographer. Cuarón shoots in gorgeous black and white - it was a privilege to watch this film on a big screen.
reviews.author: Baradwaj Rangan

reviews.text: Astoundingly, this is Aparicio's acting debut. It is a stoic, studied performance that at times pushes into realms of intense physical and emotional endurance that result in some of the film's most devastating scenes.
reviews.author: Beth Webb

reviews.text: So full of dazzlingly intricate visual poetry, so teeming with sensory spirit, that trying to review it is a bit like trying to review all of life. Which may sound a bit grandiose, but Cuarón's magnum opus provokes such turgid sentiment.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: It's fitting that Cuarón is also the cinematographer here, as Roma is a deeply personal handsome vision. Cuarón is a master at visual storytelling, pointing to a small change in the frame that will be important later on.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: Cuarón shoots in a generous widescreen that seems to take in all the sights, sounds and even smells of barrio life.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Roma is a return to more earthly delights for Cuarón but no less effort has been made by the filmmaker (nor less practical wizardry employed) to offer the viewer a sensory experience of the characters' lives.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: Too often Roma feels dramatically insipid (the family is actually profoundly boring) and unsure of what it's trying to say about Cleo's life and her status - if it's saying anything at all.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Having seemingly mastered the Hollywood blockbuster, Cuarón appears to be setting his sights on a more intimate kind of filmmaking along the lines of the cinema's great humanists, like Yasujiro Ozu or Lucretia Martel.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: [Cuarón's] extraordinary and expansive new film, Roma, is on an altogether higher plateau - a transcendent picture album of snatched (albeit hauntingly vivid) memories which dances to its own, off-kilter tune.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: [Cuarón] tables the showiness of Children of Men and Gravity in favor of ongoing restraint, creating a fresh kind of intimacy.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: It was shot... in high-resolution wide-format 65mm black and white film, the camera movements gentle, revealing all to us, both in detail and scope, with an extraordinary effect of yearning and tenderness: instantly eidetic.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: Cuarón never seeks a tidy resolution for their loving, lopsided, complicated relationship. But it's one of the reasons why Roma leaves such a deep and lasting impression.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: Roma follows in the tradition of neorealist filmmakers like Vittorio De Sica and Satyajit Ray. No one else is making movies like this today.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Cuarón has written a love letter to all the women around the world who have devoted their lives to caring for the children of the families they work for.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: Roma is made of the stuff of memory, and is the kind of film you don't forget.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: At the heart of it all is a wonderful performance from Aparicio, who brings to the role something gentle, delicate, stoic and selfless. She is the jewel of this outstanding film.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Alfonso Cuaron's Roma is an immensely moving film made by one person, for one person and it is our privilege, and almost a little bit our intrusion, to be allowed in.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: An immersive bath in some of the most luxuriantly beautiful black-and-white images you've ever seen, this is the work of a great filmmaker who exhibits absolute control and confidence in what he's doing.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: "Roma" is gorgeously done, yet you may feel gently absorbed in it more than than you're deeply moved by it.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: It works both as a personal statement and a larger philosophical humanist love letter to life itself.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

synopsis: Cleo is one of two domestic workers who help Antonio and Sofía take care of their four children in 1970s Mexico City. Complications soon arise when Antonio suddenly runs away with his mistress and Cleo finds out that she's pregnant. When Sofía decides to take the kids on vacation, she invites Cleo for a much-needed getaway to clear her mind and bond with the family.
